content:
Omar: Nimbus (enterprise) wants a very small POC to validate dropping VendorX in favor of Redwood. Must-haves: minimal client changes, identical-ish response shape, billing translation (VendorX 50-token buckets -> per-token), and security questionnaire answers incl CMK. Can we scope a 48h sprint?
Tess: +1. They emphasized two technical blockers: (1) a stateful chat flow that relies on server-side session merging, (2) some clients expect choices[].logprobs and metadata fields.
Rahul: I can own the parity harness. Ask them for the six canonical prompts + a 2-day slice of anonymized logs. I'll run deterministic runs (seed + top_k=1) and a sampling run to show variance.
Becca: I'll draft security answers. Key Qs: customer-managed KMS, IP allowlist, SOC2 evidence, audit logs, and PII redaction before S3. Need to know if they want CMK for hosted or only Dedicated/Private.
Omar: Nimbus prefers CMK on hosted if possible. Legal will likely push for Dedicated but they'd like a hosted path if we can validate controls.
infra-bot: Note: Hosted CMK requires workspace isolation and a security review. See internal runbook (internal-only).
Tess: For the session behavior: VendorX uses server-side conversation merge and implicit session continuation. Redwood uses client-supplied conversation_id + KV cache. We'll demo a tiny adapter that accepts VendorX handshake header and reconstructs session by replaying last N messages into KV.
Rahul: Parity caveat: tokenizers differ; VendorX tokenization results in slightly different counts. We'll show tokenized diffs and a billing sim that rounds up to VendorX's 50-token buckets to compute delta. Expect +/- ~5-12% variation depending on prompts.
Becca: On logprobs: returning token-level logprobs is considered sensitive. Recommend default: off. Offer compatibility-mode behind contract for Dedicated/Private with clear logging controls. Hosted logprobs only with security review. I'll call this out.
Omar: Can the adapter synthesize missing metadata fields clients expect (choices[].metadata.model_name, choices[].finish_reason)? They need minimal code changes client-side.
Tess: Yes. Adapter will map fields and include `usage.total_tokens`. We'll also offer a compat flag to include `choices[].logprobs` (nullable) if requested.
Rahul: Example adapter curl for demo:
```
curl -X POST https://demo.redwood/compat/vendorx \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer demo-token" \
  -H "X-VendorX-Session: sess-42" \
  -d '{"input_text":"Summarize last quarter","max_tokens":80}'
```
Response will be shaped to match VendorX (choices[0].text, usage.total_tokens).
Becca: KMS path: Dedicated/Private -> CMK supported. Hosted -> possible but requires workspace isolation + security approval and a ~2-4 week window. I'll detail steps and required paperwork in the Q doc.
Tess: Rate limits: VendorX enforces 120rpm with burst. Redwood hosted uses token throughput + concurrency limits. We'll propose a mapping (e.g., translate 120rpm into an equivalent token/sec throttling and provide a sample config). Include 429 + retry_after to match client behavior.
Omar: Billing sim: Rahul, can you run a converter that tokenizes with Redwood tokenizer, computes per-request token counts, then simulates VendorX bucketing and outputs p50/p95 deltas? Attach a one-slide summary.
Rahul: Will do. If they provide logs tonight I can get numbers by Wed AM.
Becca: PII redaction: For Dedicated/Private we can enable pre-ingest redaction rules (regex + NER). Hosted can enable allowlisted redaction templates but recall may vary. I'll add examples and limitations.
Tess: Latency note: adapter adds ~8-15ms for header translation and KV assemble on cache hit; cache miss adds ~40-60ms. We'll show both numbers in the demo.
Omar: Edge-case: VendorX sometimes returns choices[].logprobs with partial nulls. Some clients check for field presence only. Adapter should return the field (nullable) to avoid crashes.
Rahul: Also flag: VendorX exposes choices[].deterministic_id in some flows. We can synthesize deterministic_id from a hash of prompt+seed to help their dedup systems.
Becca: OK action items: Rahul -> parity harness + billing sim (Wed AM). Tess -> adapter prototype + demo curl (Tue PM). Becca -> security Q doc + CMK path + PII redaction notes (Tue noon). Omar -> assemble demo slide and canary-runbook.
Omar: Nimbus asked for a canary plan: start with 5% traffic, monitor response delta metrics and error rate, fall back to VendorX if mismatch rate > threshold. We'll include a rollback play in the runbook.
Tess: I'll push a minimal adapter repo link here when ready and a lightweight README showing how to enable compat mode.
Rahul: I'll also include a quick script to convert their historical invoice lines into Redwood cost estimates.
infra-bot: Reminder: enabling hosted-CMK requires securityops approval and network isolation checklist. See internal playbook.
Omar: Great. Keep updates in this thread. Nimbus wants low-friction migration; emphasize identical response shape, billing clarity, and a clear security path. Ping when artifacts land. :thumbsup:
